name: s04-morphomechanics
title: Morphomechanics
question: How do cell aspect ratio, branch topology, packing and bond strength set collective toughness and propagule size? (Q2)
hypothesis: Varying aspect ratio, branch topology, packing and bond strength predicts toughness and propagule-size distributions; mechanics backends agree on the summary observables (C4).
claim: Cell adhesion (homotypic contact energy) sets collective toughness: a clonal CPM cluster under growth-driven stress stays one cohesive propagule at strong adhesion and fractures into multiple propagules at weak adhesion. UNPROVEN until the adhesion x seed sweep is graded; aspect ratio, branch topology and cross-backend agreement (C4) are not tested here.

behavior_tests.name: propagule-toughness-predicted
behavior_tests.description: Vary cell aspect ratio, branch topology, packing and bond strength; compare mechanics backends. Decision criterion: predict toughness and propagule-size distributions.

findings.statement: In a Rust CPM clonal growth world, adhesion sets propagule toughness: seed-mean largest_cluster_fraction is 0.19 at adhesion 0, 0.57 at 0.3 and 1.0 (a single propagule) for adhesion >= 0.5; the zero-adhesion control fractures into 11-16 propagules.
findings.inferential_scope: Transient (~40-update), quasi-static readout of one CPM backend (viva-cpm); adhesion is the only swept knob (aspect ratio, topology, packing and cross-backend agreement untested). Fracture re-merges past ~80 updates.

baseline.name: baseline
baseline.note: Spatial CPM clonal cluster (Rust viva-cpm); adhesion sets homotypic contact energy. Measured at the pinned 40-update window. n_steps=40 pins the transient window (the runner ignores the composite default_n_steps).

config.title: Weak adhesion lets growth snap a cluster into propagules

propagule-toughness-predicted.detail: Seed-mean largest_cluster_fraction at the 40-update window is non-decreasing in adhesion (adh 0.0: mean lcf 0.194; adh 0.3: mean lcf 0.565; adh 0.5: mean lcf 1.000; adh 0.62: mean lcf 1.000; adh 0.75: mean lcf 1.000; adh 0.9: mean lcf 1.000; adh 0.95: mean lcf 1.000) across 3 seeds per point; the zero-adhesion control fractures (n_propagules [16, 11, 12], largest_cluster_fraction [0.078, 0.267, 0.239], all < 0.5) while adhesion >= 0.5 stays a single propagule in every seed. Per-seed series are not strictly monotone (seed 2: 0.0->0.3 0.267->0.262): graded on the seed-mean, the 0.0->0.3 seed-2 dip is within replicate noise. Transient, quasi-static readout (re-merges past ~80 updates); adhesion is the only swept knob.

verdict_rationale: Earned by a real 21-run CPM sweep (7 adhesion values x 3 potts seeds, 40-update window): seed-mean largest_cluster_fraction rises 0.19 (adhesion 0) -> 0.57 (0.3) -> 1.0 (>=0.5), and the zero-adhesion control fractures into 11-16 propagules. Provisional: transient quasi-static readout, adhesion-only sweep, one mechanics backend. The 0.62 cohesion threshold estimated in the composite spike was not seen: cohesion already holds at 0.5.
limitations: The fracture readout is a TRANSIENT, quasi-static measurement: it is taken at the pinned ~40-update window (default_n_steps=40). Past ~80 updates crowding re-merges clusters and the strong-vs-weak adhesion contrast disappears, so this is not a steady-state toughness.
Adhesion is the only mechanical knob swept; cell aspect ratio, branch topology, packing and cross-backend agreement (parts of C4) are not tested.
